clue.text: Steward — shifts deter him a lot

indicators.note: shifts means moves around, so the letters of the following words are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A head waiter's tactics for keeping a troublesome customer from coming back too often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' signals an anagram of DETERHIMALOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A head waiter runs the dining room's service staff, a kind of chief attendant in a restaurant.

clue.text: "Most fruit"., said Richard, "is sweet'

indicators.note: most of each word means its last letter is dropped from the fruit and from the name

explanation.surface: A man named Richard claims that most fruit tastes sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' trims the last letter from both MELON and DICK, giving MELO and DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodic music is tuneful and pleasing to the ear, as a sweet melody is.

clue.text: Exponents of batting taking risks

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in
dices, as in dices with death, means takes risks

explanation.surface: Advocates of reckless batting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exponents' looks like advocates; it is the mathematical sense, powers.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra the small raised numbers showing a power are called this, exponents by another name.

clue.text: Order your ball-point in colour

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: a point of the compass, here E for east

explanation.surface: Asking for your ballpoint pen in a particular ink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' rearranges YOURBALL to ROYALBLU; E (a compass point) ends it. 'ball-point' looks like a pen, but splits into ball and point.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep vivid shade, a named hue.

clue.text: Stupid, but studies English

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

explanation.surface: A dim pupil who nonetheless studies English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'studies' looks like a verb; it is the plural noun, rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense is an informal word for slow-witted or thick.

clue.text: Best gold is found in the open air

parts.note: to best someone is to outdo them
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: The finest gold is discovered out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' is a verb, to beat. OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor event takes place outside, not under a roof.

clue.text: No one has time for raising an issue

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means the run of pieces is read from the bottom up

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
tide is an old word for time, as in Christmastide

explanation.surface: Nobody has time to bring up a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for raising' turns NOITIDE upwards. 'issue' means a printed number, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one printing or release of a publication, as a magazine number is.

clue.text: Later in the same document or form, I enter the RAF

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A recruit filling in a document or application form to join the Royal Air Force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like a paper to fill in, which suits the surface; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal drafting uses this word to mean from that point onward in a text.

clue.text: Princess participating in religious festival

indicators.note: a person participating in something is inside it, so the princess's name goes inside the word for religious

parts.note: Princess Ida is the heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta of that name

explanation.surface: A royal attending a church feast day.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is the heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, a name setters use for any princess; 'participating in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday was originally a holy day, a religious feast, and still means a day of celebration off work.

clue.text: It stops the ball making a profit

explanation.surface: A cricket or tennis remark about what halts a shot, jumbled with business talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A net of mesh halts a ball in sport, and to net money is to clear it as profit after costs.

clue.text: Felt sore so had an injection

explanation.surface: Someone resentful after a jab at the doctor's.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to get the needle is to become irritated or annoyed; literally it is receiving a hypodermic jab.

clue.text: Searching for an advanced Liberal

explanation.surface: Looking about for a progressive politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Searching criticism goes to the root, thorough and fundamental; a reformer of the far left wing of the old Liberal party was called this.

clue.text: Gascon acquired one in the East of Gascony

indicators.note: the pieces for acquired and one sit in the French word for east

parts.note: Gascony is in France, where east is est
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man from south-west France picked something up in the eastern part of his region.
explanation.walkthrough: Gascons were proverbial braggarts (hence gasconade), so a Gascon is a boastful self-admirer. The East of Gascony is French: EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Gascons had a reputation as boasters, so the word came to mean a braggart, someone full of self-importance.

clue.text: Some in custody for part of the hearing

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some prisoners held for a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks legal, but it is the sense of hearing: the definition is an ear bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The anvil-shaped middle-ear ossicle passes sound vibrations toward the inner ear, so it is a component of the auditory apparatus.

clue.text: I replaced Byron's love in timber maze

indicators.note: the altered poet's name is placed in the word for timber

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of timber

indicators.note: replaced says the letter for I takes the place of the letter for love in the poet's name

parts.note: Lord Byron, the Romantic poet; the 's is no letter
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lover of Byron's lost in a wooden puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' gives BYRIN (I in place of O), which 'in' sets within the timber. 'love' is O, as zero in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A labyrinth is an intricate network of winding paths, the classical word for a puzzle of passages.

clue.text: Fat prize for one of the boat people

explanation.surface: A prize of fat for a member of a ship's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Buttercup is the bumboat woman in Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore, so she is one of its boat people.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Buttercup sells goods from a small boat in HMS Pinafore, a character among the shipboard cast.

clue.text: Lamenting stormy row

indicators.note: something stormy is turbulent, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Grieving over a tempestuous quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel, matching 'stormy'; it is a line, as in things in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Things in alignment are arranged in a straight line, as a line of objects is.

clue.text: I raced a man from Persia

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of having run against a Persian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Persia' is adjectival, matching the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia is the old name of the country now called Iran.

clue.text: Cloth makes girl enthusiastic

explanation.surface: A fabric that excites a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton fabric originally made in Nanjing.

clue.text: Dog's memorial

explanation.surface: A dog's grave marker.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn terrier is a small Scottish dog breed; a cairn is also a heap of stones raised as a landmark or monument.

clue.text: Coach of foreign game

annotationWithheld.why: Coach of foreign game (7) for CHARADE: no sound parse found; CHAR (French carriage) leaves A+DE with 'of foreign' giving only DE, so the A has no clue word

clue.text: Drive up the motorway with favourite American

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the motorway's letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, London to Leeds, written here with I for 1

explanation.surface: Driving north on the motorway with a favourite American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a verb but is a noun, momentum. The M1 is read as MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or momentum pushing something forward.

clue.text: Unusual terrain for a coach :

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of the next word are set out in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: Odd ground for a bus or sports instructor to work on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' hints at a vehicle; it is a person who trains athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports instructor who prepares athletes or a team is called this.

clue.text: Criticizes tax

explanation.surface: Complains about a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is to scold them angrily; rates were the British local property levy.

clue.text: For instance, former parliamentarian takes drink outside

indicators.note: the drink goes on the outside of the parliamentarian

parts.note: MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An ex-MP who takes a drink outside, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For instance' is the definition, matching the phrase 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'for instance' is used in the same way as 'for example', introducing an illustrative case.

clue.text: Clothing that's light, intended for auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: ray means light and meant means intended

explanation.surface: Garments described as lightweight, meant for accountants checking books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditors' suggests accountants, but it means listeners: RAY MEANT is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for garments or dress.

clue.text: Talk preceding return of rented property

indicators.note: the word for talk comes before the reversed piece
return of means the word for rented is read backwards

explanation.surface: A conversation before getting back a let house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns LET into TEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is an item of movable personal possession, in law something owned other than land.

clue.text: Not one meal eaten by very large bankrupt

indicators.note: eaten by puts the pieces inside the letters for very large

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Someone so broke that a huge person ate their only meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very large' is OS, the clothing size outsize; 'eaten by' is the container signal. 'Not one meal' reads as a single idea but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being penniless pictures shoes worn through to the top leather.
